**No — the paper gives two different numbers for it.**

For Gemini's deep-research configuration (`Gemini (DR)`), DeepTRACE reports citation accuracy as:

| Where | Figure | Severity label |
|---|---|---|
| Table 1, `%Citation Accuracy` column | **50.3%** | borderline |
| Results prose, "Deep Research Agents" paragraph | **40.3%** | problematic |

The prose reads: *"Gemini(DR) demonstrates weak citation performance: only 40.3% citation accuracy (problematic)"* — in the same sentence that gives its 27.1% thoroughness, which **is** consistent with Table 1.

So the inconsistency is confined to the accuracy figure, and it isn't a bare typo you can read past: under the paper's own Appendix B thresholds (below 50 = problematic), each number is self-consistent with the label printed next to it. A reader can't use the severity marker to work out which one is meant.

**The abstract breaks the tie in favour of 40.3%.** It states citation accuracy for deep-research configurations *"ranging from 40–80% across systems."* Table 1's deep-research rows are GPT-5 79.1, YouChat 72.3, Copilot 62.1, PPLX 58.0, and Gemini 50.3 — Gemini is the floor of that range. A 50.3% floor would make the abstract's range 50–80%, not 40–80%. Two of the three mentions therefore point at 40.3, and Table 1's 50.3 looks like the transcription error.
